_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

**Frame:** Publish `__beefy-taco-pasta.md` as written, or revise before undraft? Context: personal Instant Pot taco pasta — 1 kg lean beef + 1 kg short pasta in 8-quart; separate skillet brown; layered liquid/meat/paste; 5 min high + exactly 5 min NPR. Stakes: burn notices, soggy pasta, salt bombs, readers in smaller pots — recipe credibility on a Food post.

### White / First Principles
**Known:** Layering (pasta → liquid → meat → paste sauce → mushrooms, no pre-stir) matches Instant Pot burn-sensor logic. Separate skillet brown removes fond/deglaze from the cook path. ~1.65 L broth per 1 kg dried short pasta is a real ratio claim (~1.65 ml/g). Half box-time → 5 min HP is standard IP pasta heuristic. 5+5 release is a texture control, not folklore. 6-quart called out as half-batch only.

**Unknown / checkable:** Actual pot fill height at 1 kg pasta + 1.65 L + 1 kg meat + 650 g mushrooms vs 8-quart max-fill. Exact taco seasoning salt load (brand/packet variance). Whether 95% lean + no cornstarch still yields a sauce that clings after toss, or stays brothy until cheese. Reproducibility of “exactly 5 min NPR” across models (float-valve behavior differs). Tomato paste 170–180 ml range vs held-back 120 ml — thickness at pour. No yield weight, no salt amount beyond “taste after,” no tested brands named.

**Assumption to strip:** “Cookbook I started from” is not a method citation readers can verify.

### Red / Instinct
ATK gut: batch feels like a house recipe that works in *one* kitchen, not a tested formula. IP gut: layering and burn warnings land — this person has fought the sensor. Still nervous about 1 kg pasta packed to the lid and “exactly 5 minutes” as gospel. Cotija *or* pepper Jack at the end feels like two different dinners. Want a photo of the layered pot before seal, not another template hero.

### Black / Contrarian
**Ship this unrevised and you own three failure modes.**

1. **Max-fill is the fatal miss.** ATK would not publish a 1:1 kilo batch for “8-quart if you stay under the line” without a measured fill photo or a hard “if above X, remove Y grams pasta.” Readers who ignore the warning get Foil Fail / Burn / unsafe overfill. Soft warning ≠ tested ceiling.

2. **Seasoning is uncontrolled.** “~100 g taco seasoning, no cornstarch” plus broth/powder is a salt lottery. ATK would weigh salt in the mix or name a tested blend + sodium ballpark. “Taste after tossing” is late for Instant Pot — you cannot un-salt a sealed cycle.

3. **Pasta science is half-told.** Half box time works for many shapes; campanelle vs penne vs rigatoni absorb differently at the same 5+5. Claiming one number for six shapes without “if box says 12+, use 6” invites mush or chalk. NPR “exactly 5” also fights real life: kids, doorbell, float valve — soft noodles get blamed on broth when the clock slipped.

4. **Separate skillet is honest but costly.** Weeknight “one-pot” framing fights an extra dirty pan. Fine if owned; weak if sold as Instant Pot convenience without saying the trade.

5. **Texture finish is vague.** “If soupy, lid 1–2 min off heat” is a patch, not a test outcome. ATK would state expected sauce state at open (glossy / pool / dry) so readers know they landed.

### Yellow / Expansionist
If this works as written, it is a **crowd-batch Instant Pot playbook** that scales past the usual 450 g recipe — rare, useful, shareable. Layering + no-thickener + separate brown is a teachable anti-burn system readers can steal for other pasta dumps. Mushrooms-on-top steam is a smart swap for bell-pepper mush. Metric-first with US cups is ATK-adjacent clarity for global readers. Leftover reheat note closes the loop for real households. Voice already sounds like someone who burned a pot and fixed it — that trust sells Food better than sterile lab tone. Publish after one fill-line photo and one salt note and this becomes a go-to archive recipe, not a one-off draft.

### Green / Options
1. **Do nothing / ship draft as-is** — keep personal house recipe; accept variance; hope max-fill + “taste after” covers you.
2. **ATK-lite revise (default better path)** — add: tested seasoning brand or DIY spice weights + salt grams; fill-line photo or “remove pasta until below line”; shape table (box time → HP minutes); expected open texture; half-batch 6-quart card.
3. **IP-purist revise** — brown in pot, deglaze, then layer (true one-pot); retune liquid; accept more burn risk teaching.
4. **Split posts** — short “how I layer IP pasta” tip + thinner recipe card; less essay, more checklist.

### Outsider
Stranger sees: long personal essay about not burning dinner, then a huge family batch that “only fits 8-quart,” mystery taco packets, and a template image. Weird: related notes are habit/productivity, not food. Weird: Cotija *or* Jack with no preference. Weird: “Glad this…” bookends without saying who ate it or how many times it was cooked. Reads half blog confession, half scaled cookbook page — stranger unsure whether to trust numbers or the story.

### Executor
**Monday step:** Cook the full 1 kg batch once with a ruler/phone photo at max-fill *before* sealing, weigh the exact seasoning used, write one line for sauce look at open. That single cook decides what to cut or keep.

### Self-review
1. **Strongest:** Black — max-fill, salt, and shape timing are the real publish blockers.
2. **Blind spot:** No blind taste / food-safety angle (ground beef “mostly browned” then pressure — fine under pressure, but ATK would say “to 160°F / no pink after toss” for nervous readers).
3. **Missed by all:** Cost per serving, allergen/swap list (no dairy option beyond skip cheese), and whether chicken broth fights “taco” flavor vs beef broth.

### Blue / Chairman

## Where the lenses agree
Layering + no cornstarch + separate brown is sound Instant Pot practice. Batch size and 5+5 timing need tighter guardrails before undraft. Personal voice is an asset, not the problem.

## Where the lenses clash
Yellow wants to ship the teachable anti-burn system soon. Black refuses publish until fill, salt, and pasta-shape variance are pinned. Green’s “do nothing” only works if this stays forever-draft house notes.

## Blind spots
Doneness cue after pressure; broth type vs taco flavor; related_notes mismatch; hero still `image-template.jpg` (anti-slop hard block).

## The recommendation
**Do not undraft yet.** Keep method and ratios; revise like ATK staff would insist and Instant Pot cooks would thank you: prove the 8-quart fill, lock seasoning/salt, and disambiguate pasta timing by box time. Separate skillet stays — say it upfront as the burn-avoidance tax, not pretend one-pot purity. After one instrumented cook + photo, this is publishable.

## The one thing to do first
Run the full 1 kg batch once: photo at max-fill before seal, note exact seasoning weight/brand and sauce look at open — then edit those three facts into the post.
